requests.prompt:
IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE ITEM SHEET. Return exactly one image, nothing else.

WHAT THIS IS
A sheet of 16 small items for "The Adventures of Tom", a family role-playing game. The game shows each item in a banner when the player receives it, so each item is one clear object that reads at a glance. The attached picture shows the painting style: take only how it is painted, and paint only the objects in the list below.

LAYOUT
- A grid of 4 columns by 4 rows of equal square cells, filled left to right, top to bottom, in the order of the list. No grid lines, no borders, no numbers, no labels.
- Exactly 16 objects, one per cell, each complete and centered, filling about 70 percent of its cell with at least 12 percent empty margin on every side. Nothing touches or crosses a cell edge, and nothing overlaps.
- Background: one flat solid #FF00FF magenta everywhere, with no magenta inside any object.

STYLE
- Hand-painted by hand: visible brushwork, matte painted surfaces, rich warm colors, crisp painted edges, gently simplified friendly shapes. Warm golden light from the upper left, shadow on the lower right of each form, no cast shadow on the ground.
- No thick or black outlines. NOT pixel art, NOT retro game art, NOT photorealistic, NOT a 3D render, NOT glossy plastic.
- Three-quarter view from slightly above, unless the list says laid flat or standing. All objects share one lighting direction and one level of detail. Family friendly for children aged 6 and up.

RULES
- Draw exactly the 16 objects in the list, one per cell, and never substitute, add or skip one. Where a list entry is unusual, draw it as written.
- Objects only: no people, no hands, no faces on anything unless the list says the object has them (a plush toy, a pot with eyes).
- No readable words or letters anywhere. Where an object normally carries print, paint soft blurred squiggles instead. A single bold numeral is allowed only where the list asks for it.
- No real brands, logos or copyrighted characters.

THE 16 ITEMS (cell number: name, what to paint)
1. Straw Sunhat: A wide-brimmed straw sunhat with a plain ribbon band, seen from a three-quarter angle.
2. Sunny Shirt: A short-sleeved bright sunny yellow t-shirt, folded flat and seen from the front.
3. Pocket Trousers: Khaki trousers with four big pockets, seen flat from the front, one pocket button undone.
4. Walking Shoes: A pair of worn canvas walking shoes with frayed laces, side by side.
5. Pocket Notebook: A small pocket notebook with a worn brown cover, an elastic band and a pencil tucked in the spine.
6. Smooth Pebble: One smooth round grey river pebble with a pale stripe, the size of an egg.
7. Spare Button: One chunky round shiny button with four holes, in dark teal with a loose thread.
8. Warm Roll: A warm crusty bread roll with a golden top and a little steam rising.
9. Overdue Bookmark: A long cloth bookmark ribbon in plum purple with a tassel, a little crumpled, peeking out of nothing.
10. Steve (a sprout): A tiny green sprout with two leaves in a small terracotta pot, standing very upright.
11. Potato Stamp: A potato cut in half with a simple carved star on the flat face, brown ink on the star, and a wooden handle.
12. Dramatic Biscuit: A big round golden biscuit with a dramatic bite taken out of it and a few crumbs.
13. Star Chart Scrap: A torn scrap of dark blue star chart paper with gold dot stars and thin gold lines.
14. Lavender Tee: A soft lavender t-shirt with a faint sparkle all over, folded flat.
15. Flower Pants: Black leggings covered in tiny pastel flowers, folded flat.
16. Purple Sneakers: A pair of purple sneakers with white soles that glow with little light-up dots on the heels.
